title: blf.c: Convert XML processing to use libxml2
description:
Convert the "home grown" XML parsing to use the libxml2 API.

Ping #20508

notes.body: @giovanni.musto - What do you think of this MR?  I found a few BLF files, but it sounds like you may have more files to test with.
This is unnecessary. As far as I know, the XML channels metadata starts right with the XML, so you can just call `xmlParseMemory` on the entire length.

Unfortunately that's not true (I originally tried that).  One of the first captures I came across (see #19380 ) didn't have this and XMLlib2 seems to be picky about the parsing.  That's partially why I wanted you to look at the patch, hopefully XMLlib2 isn't too rigid (or my implementation of it) to have capture files that "used to work" with the old scheme, but not the new one.
I remember only seeing the BOM in some files, and I think libxml2 should handle it. Anyways, let's keep compatibility whenever possible.
Yes, that is the problem. We can just pass `text` and `apptextheader.textLength` to `blf_set_xml_channels`, and free `text` later.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20015/diffs?diff_id=1375308192&start_sha=4508df83e89799daa9dfd2df92402320b42dd2d9#4edaab23888743307322f501fbaef9f54209f5e5_3009_3007)
Done
Here, if `str_channel != NULL` but `ws_strtou16` returned false, the string will not be freed.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20015/diffs?diff_id=1375110756&start_sha=596b8004ae04865d2f58efd289869deee80e20c3#4edaab23888743307322f501fbaef9f54209f5e5_3055_3056)
Good catch.

Thanks for the contribution. After a quick review it looks like everything is fine. I will try the commit locally later today to see how it behaves with my files.

In the meanwhile, please take a look at the problems found by the automatic build.
